guidance: p > 0.05 means no leftover serial structure. Failing it points to a missing seasonal or trend component, not to a wrong effect.
Affects the model's own interval only. The conformal interval used here does not assume normality, so this is informational.
Large |acf1| means the local level is absorbing structure the covariates should explain.
Mean absolute forecast error over 20 rolling origins. Above 5% the counterfactual is too loose to price a campaign.
Fewer than ~10 origins makes the error distribution -- and therefore the interval -- unreliable.
Adding a noise predictor should move the estimate by well under a point. A large shift means the adjustment set is doing unstable work.
A noise outcome must not yield a significant effect. The point estimate is free to wander; the interval must contain zero.
Re-estimating on 20% less history should not move the answer much. If it does, the result is a property of the window chosen.
